A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Low-Rank Thinning and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–L. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 4.2, 5.2, and 6.2 report original attention-approximation, mortgage-classification SGD, and Higgs two-sample-testing experiments.

after.justification: v6 retains these experiments and adds BigGAN evaluation in Table 4 and empirical structural analyses in Figures L.1–L.2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the appendix thinning procedures remain unchanged. BigGAN evaluates the existing Thinformer procedure; the added explanations and revised theoretical bounds do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds BigGAN image generation, extending attention evaluation beyond T2T-ViT image classification to a distinct generative task. Mortgage classification and Higgs testing remain covered.

E2.justification: Exact attention, Performer, Reformer, KDEformer, and ScatterBrain remain the attention comparators and are extended to BigGAN. Comparator membership in the retained SGD and Higgs experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new BigGAN experiment introduces FID/IS evaluation, 32-image timing batches, and benchmark-specific attention configurations. Figure L.2 adds a sample-size sweep from 4^3 to 4^7 with fixed beta, s, and g. Retained experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v6 adds two analyses directly examining the low-rank premise: per-epoch gradient ranks and a singular-value spectrum in Figure L.1, and empirical CTT error-inflation scaling in Figure L.2. v5 contains neither diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Table 4 adds BigGAN timing-replication information: mean and one standard deviation across 10 batches. Existing ImageNet and SGD seed counts and Higgs standard-error reporting remain unchanged; increased repetitions of retained experiments are not documented.

E6.justification: Table 3 and Figures 1–2 are unchanged. New Table 4 reports Thinformer FID 30.54, IS 57.12, and runtime 2.66 ms; exact attention has higher IS, 58.37, while Performer is faster at 2.28 ms. Figures L.1–L.2 add rank and scaling findings, including median gradient rank 10 versus ambient dimension 19.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 and Lemma G.2 revise the SGD rank threshold and associated constants, changing the stated approximation scale from O(1/sqrt(n)) to O(log(Kn)/sqrt(n)). Section 3 also adds a minimax argument for GS-THIN. The central low-rank, attention, and CTT theorems and their proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is identical, and the introduction and closing Impact Statement retain the same low-rank-analysis contribution and three application areas. The added experiments support these headline claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New passages interpret the SGD and Higgs findings as direct verification of theoretical guarantees and connect the appendix diagnostics to approximate low-rankness. Section 4.2 also adds interpretation of BigGAN's quality–runtime tradeoff, including Performer's greater speed but poorer generation quality.

D1.justification: Appendix L.1 and Table L.2 document BigGAN-specific software, A6000 hardware, attention dimensions, warm-up procedure, and comparator hyperparameters. Existing experiment details and code-access links are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds Heusel et al. (2017) and Salimans et al. (2016) for generation metrics. It also explicitly positions GS-THIN, SGD, and CTT guarantees against lower bounds from already cited Phillips–Tai, Cha et al., and Kim–Schrab work.

P1.justification: v6 adds an introductory roadmap, algorithm intuition, proof-strategy explanations, and labels for SGD assumptions. It removes duplicated attention-bound displays in favor of Table 2 references. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v6 substantially extends the displayed evidence with BigGAN results and configuration tables, Table 4 and Table L.2, plus rank, spectrum, and scaling plots in Figures L.1–L.2. Existing tables and performance plots are retained, with surrounding layout reflow.

improvement.justification: BigGAN evaluation broadens practical validation, while Figures L.1–L.2 provide useful checks of the low-rank premise missing from v5. Added implementation details and clearer explanations improve reproducibility and accessibility. These benefits outweigh limited overinterpretation: finite plots alone do not establish the newly asserted direct verification of guarantees or asymptotic growth.
